summary: Friedberg argues Anthropic is worth significantly more than its $350B mark due to explosive ARR growth (~$6B added in a month) and the viral adoption of Claude/Cowork, making it a strong multiple-expansion bet even amid the Pentagon controversy.
quote: Anthropic is worth a lot more than $350. That's for sure. They just added $6 billion in the last month. And I will tell you anecdotally, everyone I talk to is on Cowork... Anthropic may actually be fulfilling the promise of AI.

summary: Friedberg warns that Google's imminent integration of a Cowork-like coding agent into G Suite poses a serious competitive threat that could sweep the market away from Anthropic within ~90 days.
quote: It's only gonna take 90 days for Google to flip on a virtual version of Cowork. And once Google has this integrated with G Suite... I think Google sweeps the market with this same competitor.

scoreNote: Explicitly named as the top pick in a forced-choice between OpenAI, Anthropic, and Google; 'Google is the bet'
summary: Friedberg picks Google as the best net market value creator among AI plays, citing its own cloud infrastructure (lower margins vs. Anthropic), G Suite distribution advantage, and imminent Cowork-like agent rollout.
quote: I think Google is the bet. I think Google is the market value creator bet, but I think Anthropic is the multiple bet. I think Anthropic is a trillion five market cap at the end of the day, unless this blows them up.

summary: Emil Michael highlights Anduril as a prime beneficiary of the shift from legacy defense primes to low-cost, mass-producible unmanned systems, and wants them to win big contracts quickly to grow the defense-tech flywheel.
quote: Androl, sure... warfare is going from big carrier ships that cost $20 billion and a decade and a half to build to mass, attritable, low-cost things. And that's what these new entrants can do.

summary: Chamath argues Anthropic's politically-driven terms-of-service decisions and reliability risk make it an untrustworthy enterprise vendor, and that the Pentagon feud has alienated both Republican and progressive constituents, threatening its business model.
quote: Anthropic just lost all the Republicans, but I think that if they think that they have the Democrats, that's fleeting as well... in both ways, I think they accidentally may have pissed off every constituent.
